subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: High blood sugar episode
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 55 years old, male. I was brought in because I had a really high blood sugar and they had to treat me for that. I think it was because I wasn't monitoring my sugar intake as much and there's been a lot of stress lately. Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and provide more details about your recent high blood sugar episode, including when it occurred and any symptoms you experienced? Patient: I'm 55, male. The high blood sugar was a few days ago, and I wasn't really watching what I ate much. I've been pretty stressed with all the events and visitors we've had, and I think that didn't help. I didn't have any symptoms other than feeling a bit off, but they had to treat me for it in the ER. Doctor: Could you provide details about your diabetes diagnosis, including when it was diagnosed, the type of diabetes (if known), and any medications or treatments you have been on? Patient: I wasn't actually diagnosed with diabetes yet, but they did find a really high blood sugar level and treated me in the ER. They put me on metformin, which I think is a medication for diabetes. I'm still figuring out what's going on, but I'm here to talk about it. Doctor: Could you share the specific blood glucose levels that were recorded during your recent episode, and have you had any follow-up tests such as HbA1c or fasting blood glucose tests since your ER visit? Patient: They actually did give me a lot of fluid in the emergency room, and my blood sugar was 162 when they checked it recently. I had eaten about two hours before that. They also did an HbA1c test, and it came back at 8, which they said is higher than it was before. Doctor: Could you provide more details about your family history of diabetes or cardiovascular disease, as well
